questions.q: What is an electromagnet?
a: A magnet made by wrapping insulated wire around a magnetic core (like iron) and passing an electric current through it
A rare mineral found naturally deep underground
A permanent magnet made of hardened steel
A device that creates electricity without energy

questions.q: What is the main advantage of an electromagnet over a permanent magnet?
a: Electromagnets never need any power source
Electromagnets can be turned on and off and their strength can be adjusted
Electromagnets are always weaker than permanent magnets
Electromagnets work only in freezing temperatures

questions.q: Which of the following components is required to build a basic working electromagnet?
a: A glass rod, water, and a battery
A wooden stick and a plastic thread
A power source (battery), insulated copper wire, and a magnetic core (such as an iron nail)
A solar panel and a mirror

questions.q: How can you increase the strength of an electromagnet?
a: Use a plastic core instead of iron
Decrease the number of wire coils
Unplug the battery
Increase the electric current, add more turns of wire to the coil, or use a soft iron core

questions.q: What happens to an electromagnet when the electric current flowing through its coil is switched off?
a: It loses its magnetism almost immediately
It becomes a permanent magnet forever
Its poles reverse direction
It turns into a light bulb

questions.q: What happens to the magnetic poles of an electromagnet if you reverse the direction of the electric current flowing through the coil?
a: The magnet explodes
The North and South poles swap places
The magnetic strength doubles
The magnet loses all power

questions.q: Which of the following everyday devices uses an electromagnet in its operation?
a: A wooden kitchen spoon
A glass window pane
An electric bell, relay, or scrap yard crane
A non-stick frying pan

questions.q: Why is soft iron used as the core inside an electromagnet rather than hardened steel?
a: Soft iron is cheaper to mine
Soft iron is a better electrical insulator
Soft iron makes the wire heavier
Soft iron magnetizes and demagnetizes easily, meaning the core doesn't stay magnetized when power is switched off

questions.q: How does a scrap metal recycling yard crane use an electromagnet?
a: To pick up heavy iron and steel objects easily when switched on, and drop them instantly when switched off
To melt scrap metal with heat
To weigh vehicles on scales

questions.q: What is the function of the insulated coating on the copper wire used to make an electromagnet coil?
a: To make the wire look colorful
To prevent short circuits by stopping current from leaking directly between touching loops of wire
To increase air resistance
To store chemical energy

questions.q: If you double the number of turns of wire in an electromagnet coil while keeping the current constant, what happens to its magnetic strength?
a: The magnetic strength drops to zero
The magnetic strength is halved
The magnetic strength increases significantly
The magnetic strength remains unchanged

questions.q: What role does an electromagnetic relay play in a large electrical circuit?
a: It consumes all excess electricity
It converts electrical energy into sound waves
It acts as a mechanical brake

questions.q: How does an electric bell use an electromagnet to produce a ringing sound?

The bell heats up until it melts
Electricity flows through a hollow chime

questions.q: What happens to the strength of an electromagnet if you increase the voltage of the battery powering it?
a: The strength decreases because voltage resists magnetism
The strength increases because a higher voltage drives a larger electric current through the coils
The strength stays completely constant
The wire melts into gas

questions.q: Which of the following devices relies on electromagnets to convert electrical signals into sound waves in music speakers or headphones?
a: A digital thermometer
A handheld calculator

questions.q: Why are electromagnets used in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) machines in hospitals?
a: To X-ray broken bones with light

To cool down patients' bodies

The wire turns into a permanent magnet
The current stops flowing entirely

a: To create friction against rails
To lift and propel the train using magnetic repulsion and attraction, eliminating wheel-on-rail friction
To generate steam power
To cool the train's engine

Albert Einstein
Hans Christian Oersted
Thomas Edison

questions.q: Why are electromagnets preferred over permanent magnets on industrial assembly line cranes that sort metallic waste?

Permanent magnets cannot be turned off to release the collected metal objects

a: To play music
